newsitem.title: UK: Gene crop labelling not practical -Canada minister.
newsitem.headline: Gene crop labelling not practical -Canada minister.

text.p: Labelling food products which contain genetically modified crops is not practical, according to Canada's minister responsible for crops, Ralph Goodale.
"I don't think it is a practical solution," he told reporters at a world grain conference in London on Thursday.

The European Union's executive Commission on Wednesday formally approved compulsory labelling of all genetically modified farm products from July 31, specifying that the product "may contain or consist of genetically modified organisms".
Goodale described the logistical problems involved in segregating such crops in the distribution chain as a huge challenge.
It would add around 10 percent to the cost of supplies of Canadian canola, or rapeseed, said an official accompanying Goodale at the International Grains Council conference.
